3. The defendant Nos. 1-4 and 7-13 entered appearance in the suit and filed written statement denying all the materials allegations of the plaint contending interalia, that Asiruddin Mallik, the predecessors of the plaintiffs on 20th Jaistha, 1339 BS by an unregistered deed sold the suit land to one Babor Ali, the predecessors of the defendants and after the death of the said Babor Ali, the defendants as his legal heirs inherited the suit land and thereupon, the SA record has been published correctly in their name including the names of their predecessor and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. Mr Humayun Kabir, further submits that PW 2 proved 2 registered kabala deeds, rent receipts but the Courts below committed wrong in discarding the same without assigning any reason whatsoever which occasioned a failure of justice. The learned Advocate then referring to the evidence of PWs submits that both the Courts below did not at all consider the evidence of PWs namely, PW 1, PW 2, PW 3 and PW 4 in its true perspective since all them testified in one voice that the plaintiffs are in possession over the suit land and PW 2, proved the registered kabala deeds dated 13-1-87 and 1-4-87 as Exhibit Nos. 3 and 3(Ka). Drawing my attention to the evidence of DWs namely DW and DW 2 Mr Humayun Kabir points out that the DWs are not only made inconsistent statement with regard to their so-called unregistered kabala deed they also could not produce any document in support of their so-called unregistered deed before the trial Court but in spite of that the Courts below most illegally relying on the evidence of DWs dismissed the suit on the ground that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession over the suit land. Mr Humayun Kabir, relying on the decision reported in 19 DLR 9 and 59 DLR 207 submits that the defendants claimed their right, title over the suit and on the basis of SA record which appears to be prepared wrongly in their name at the early period of the than Pakistan but such record of rights does neither create nor destroy the right, title and possession as acquired by the plaintiff-petitioners on the basis of two registered kabala deeds dated 13-1-87 and 1-4-87 as Exhibit Nos. 3 and 3(Ka). He further adds that the SA record is not a conclusive evidence which is mere a record of physical possession at the time when it is prepared. 

 14. Now, let me discuss the evidence of PWs in order to resolve the issue whether the impugned judgments of two Courts below are based on correct and proper appreciation of the evidence and materials on record on the point of possession. On going through the materials on record, it appears that plaintiff No. 1, Esahaq Ali Mallik himself was examined as PW 1, who stated that after the death of Asiruddin Mallik his heirs namely Maju Bibi (wife), 4 (four) daughters namely Faku, Maju, Saju and Moyna and one son Jabbar inherited the suit land and Faku, Maju and Saju Bibi transferred 0.36 acres of land to the plaintiffs by a registered deed and Moyna Bibi also transferred her portion of land by executing another registered kabala deed. This witness also stated that after execution of the deeds they handed over the possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs. This witness also stated that : 

 "আমরা সম্পূর্ণ জমি ভোগ দখল করি । " PW 2, Mosharraf Mallik, who stated that : " সাজু, মাজু আমার প্রতিবেশী এবং একই বয়সের মেয়ে । সাজু, মাজু, ফকু বিবি ৩ জনে জমি ১/২ নং বাদীদের বরাবর কবলা দেয় । তাও জানি । আমি পরিচিত ছিলাম । ৪ বৎসর আগে পৌষ মাসের শেষে দিকে দখল দেয় । সাজু, মাজু এবং ফকু বিবি আমার সামনে টিপ দেয় ।  " 

 PW-3, Sabed Ali Sheikh, stated that Moyna Bibi is her cousin's wife, who transferred the suit land to the plaintiffs. He identified the signature of Moyna Bibi and proved her signature as Exhibit 'Ka'. This witness in his cross-examination denied the suggestion that the possession of the suit land was not handed over infamous of the plaintiffs.  17. It is found from the evidence of the defendant witnesses that DW 1, Tobarek Sheikh, in his deposition stated that their un-registered deed was written on 2(two) blank papers but DW 2, Mr Aladdin Sheikh in his deposition stated that their un-registered deed was written on 1 (one) blank paper. On the face of these inconsistencies, it is difficult to rely upon their testimony. It is also found that the trial Court as well as appellate Court below as last Court of fact having not been addressed this aspect of the case. 

 18. It is also found that defendants did not or could not produce their unregistered deed on the plea that during liberation war their unregistered deed was looted away. It appears that DW 1, in his cross-examination stated that with regard to missing their deed relating to the suit land he did not make any general diary. The Court of appeal below on this point observed as follows : 

 21. In the case of Abdul Jabbar vs Abdul Aziz reported in 19 DLR 9, it has been held that : "It is not certainly conclusive evidence of the state of things appearing in the record of right, or in other words, it is not conclusive evidence of correctness of the entries in the record of rights." 

 22. In the case of Dhaka City Corporation vs Shamsur Rahman reported in 59 DLR 207, wherein it has been held that : "Such view of the trial Court was reversed rightly by the appellate Court. Because, the decision of the trial Court is based on no authority. Earlier, wrong record of rights could be corrected by a mere application under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. In such proceeding, the aggrieved party was never required to establish title to get an order for correction of the record of rights. Reason is not far away to find. Record of rights does neither create nor destroy title. It is mere a record of physical possession at the time when it is prepared." 

 26. I have already indicated that in this case the plaintiff-petitioners by adducing sufficient evidence both oral and documentary proved their right, title and possession in the suit land. The secondary evidence of a document is admissible in the cases specially mentioned in section 65 of the Evidence Act and if the original is not available, reasons for non-availability must be given but in this case, I have already noticed that the defendants neither produced their unregistered deed nor produced any documentary evidence to show that their original un-registered deed in lost More so, as I have already observed the DW 1, Tobarek Sheikh, in his deposition stated that their un-registered deed was written on 2(two) blank papers and DW 2, Md Aladdin Sheikh stated in his deposition stated that their un-registered deed was written on 1(one) blank paper. These contradictions and inconstancies on material point in the facts of the present case create serious doubt upon the genuineness of the alleged unregistered deed of the defendant-opposite parties. It is also found that the Courts below did not address to this most important aspect of the case at all.
